page: Amazon Web Services c7i.48xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features dual Intel Xeon 8488C processors offering 96 physical cores and 192 vCPUs running at a base clock speed of 3.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system provides 384 GB of DDR5 memory clocked at 5 GHz, maintaining a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio with 2.0 GB of memory per core. Cache resources include 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 105 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 support alongside Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions.

The instance is equipped with a 50 Gbps baseline network interface and includes no bundled local NVMe storage, requiring persistent and scratch storage to be attached remotely. In synthetic CPU benchmarks, the platform demonstrates top-tier multi-threaded processing power, reaching 169,731.29 in stress-ng multi-core tests and a PassMark CPU score of 123,408.48, bolstered by specialized instruction sets scoring 191,847.05 on PassMark extended instructions. In-memory operations show high throughput, recording 176.17 million operations per second on Redis SET tests and 115.71 GB/sec in static web serving benchmarks. Single-core performance sits in the strong-to-average tier, represented by a Geekbench single-core score of 2,055.0.

By pairing massive parallel CPU execution density with DDR5 memory, the instance delivers high compute efficiency per core for distributed and multithreaded jobs without paying for excess memory capacity. However, the absence of integrated local storage and GPU acceleration means data-heavy I/O workloads rely completely on external network-attached volumes. AWS c7i.48xlarge is suited for high-density compute tasks including batch processing, large-scale Clang software compilation, ray tracing, in-memory data processing, high-volume web serving clusters, and CPU-based machine learning inference utilizing AMX extensions.
description: Amazon Web Services c7i.48xlarge is a compute-optimized instance driven by 96 physical cores and 192 vCPUs of Intel Xeon 8488C silicon at 3.2 GHz, paired with 384 GB of DDR5 memory. Powered by the Nitro hypervisor, the platform provides a dedicated 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, a 105 MB L3 cache, and support for AVX-512 and AMX instructions. The instance provides 50 Gbps baseline networking and excludes bundled local storage as well as GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluation exhibits top-tier multi-threaded compute and in-memory processing, highlighted by a PassMark CPU rating of 123,408.48 and over 176 million Redis SET operations per second. Hardware resources favor parallel CPU-bound density over raw memory footprint, offering efficient throughput for large-scale distributed compilation, CPU-based matrix inference, scientific computing, ray tracing, and static web serving pipelines.
